content.content:
654-
655-If a modifier isn't present, any declaration depending on a modifier is just not included in the output.
656-
657-#### Fractions
658-
659-To handle fractions, we rely on the CSS `ratio` data type. If this is used with `--value()`, it's a signal to Tailwind to treat the value and modifier as a single value:
660-
661-```css
662-/* [!code filename:CSS] */
663-@utility aspect-* {
664-  /* [!code word:ratio, \[ratio\]] */
665-  /* prettier-ignore */
666-  aspect-ratio: --value(--aspect-ratio-*, ratio, [ratio]);
667-}
668-```
669-
670-This will match utilities like `aspect-square`, `aspect-3/4`, and `aspect-[7/9]`.
671-
672-## Adding custom variants
673-
674:In addition to using the variants that ship with Tailwind, you can also add your own custom variants using the `@custom-variant` directive:
675-
676-```css
677:@custom-variant theme-midnight {
678-  &:where([data-theme="midnight"] *) {
679-    @slot;
680-  }
681-}
682-```
683-
684-Now you can use the `theme-midnight:<utility>` variant in your HTML:
685-
686-```html
687-<!-- [!code classes:theme-midnight:bg-black] -->
688-<html data-theme="midnight">
689-  <button class="theme-midnight:bg-black ..."></button>
690-</html>
691-```
692-
693-You can create variants using the shorthand syntax when nesting isn't required:
694-
695-```css
696:@custom-variant theme-midnight (&:where([data-theme="midnight"] *));
697-```
698-
699-When a custom variant has multiple rules, they can be nested within each other:
700-
701-```css
702:@custom-variant any-hover {
703-  @media (any-hover: hover) {
704-    &:hover {
705-      @slot;
706-    }
707-  }
708-}
709-```
